minors.evidence: Crop of page 6 at x140-1700, y360-1040: 'Quickly.' is at about x430-600, y330-440, and 'Others.' at about x1320-1480, y240-340. Open flames burn in brass bowls along the pillars.

minors.description: The setting drifts within the page. 7.1 and 7.2 show a narrow ladder with rungs, but 7.3 shows a broad staircase with wide treads. A hanging brass oil lamp with an open flame replaces the glass lanterns of 7.1 and 7.2. The prisoners are bare-chested in white loincloths, not the grey, brown and off-white rags seen everywhere else. The same staircase already appears in 2.4.
minors.evidence: Crop of page 7 at x920-1700, y1420-1880: stair treads at bottom centre, a brass lamp at left, and bare-chested prisoners at upper right.

minors.description: The falling guard's costume changes from 7.1. In 7.1 he wears dark brown breeches under the buff jerkin with a cream shirt. In 7.2 his breeches and underlayer are maroon-red, which also pushes toward the red that the guard rules forbid.
minors.evidence: Zoomed crop of page 7 at x320-520, y1580-1850: maroon-red cloth on the legs and the body under the morion. In 7.1 the same guard's legs are dark brown.

minors.description: The guard's helmet is a round, wide-brimmed kettle hat, not the morion with upturned peaks and crest that the script and the other guard panels use (2.2, 6.5, 7.1). He also wears a waist belt with a large buckle under the cross-belt, and the script specifies no wide belt so he cannot read as João.
minors.evidence: Crop of page 1 at x140-1700, y1600-2110: a flat circular brim around the whole helmet, and a buckled waist belt at about x520-600, y380.

minors.description: The collar ring is at the front throughout the chapter, not 'a ring at the side' as the bible's Chapter 3 row and script 1.1 specify. From the front ring, a chain hangs straight down the chest into the lap. On page 2 both men also have extra chains running from wrist irons to ankle irons, which the rig does not include.
minors.evidence: Page 1 crop at x140-1700, y360-1020: the ring is under Nagoji's chin with a chain dropping to his lap. The same front ring appears in 5.3, 10.1 and 10.3. Page 2 crop at y360-1070: vertical chains link the manacles to the ankle cuffs on both men.

minors.description: The musket is not drawn the same way from panel to panel. In 2.1 it has a rounded brass butt cap and brass lock furniture. In 2.4 it has an iron-bound butt with a plain iron lock. In 6.3 it gains a brass barrel band. Page 2 plants this musket for page 6, so it should stay the same.
minors.evidence: Page 2 crop at y360-1070 (2.1): a brass-capped cylindrical butt at bottom right. Crop at y2275-2545 (2.4): an iron butt plate. Page 6 crop at x920-1700, y1045-1725: a brass band on the barrel.

minors.description: The musket comes up out of a round wooden tub or barrel of water, not off the flooded floor at the foot of the ladder where 6.2 places it (a dark shape under thigh-deep water).
minors.evidence: Crop of page 6 at x920-1700, y1045-1725: the curved rim of a wooden tub runs along the bottom of the panel under the dripping musket.

minors.description: The crew changes costume from 8.1. Here the sailors wear dark waistcoats, and the central figure wears a black tricorne-style hat, which reads as pirate or uniform. The script and 8.1 have loose shirts and slops with knitted caps or head cloths.
minors.evidence: Zoomed crop of page 8 at x165-800, y1700-2020: waistcoats on three men and a cocked hat on the centre figure.

minors.description: The rain-washed graze at Keshavrao's hairline, the softened stand-in for the novel's head wound, is missing here and in 9.3. The caption 'For a moment I was nowhere...' is lettered at top right over the main image, not inside the inset of Nagoji's hand as the script directs.
minors.evidence: Zoomed crop of page 9 at x800-1400, y370-870: a clean forehead under wet hair. The caption box sits at about x750-1150 on the page, outside the inset at upper left.

minors.description: Nagoji's costume drifts from 9.2 to 10.4. The sleeveless ochre tunic becomes a long, shredded robe with sleeve-like drapes over both arms, and in 9.2 the cream dhoti barely shows, with bare thighs at the knee. The captivity sheet is a sleeveless tunic over a cream dhoti.
minors.evidence: Page 9, panels 9.2 to 9.4, and page 10, panel 10.4: ochre rags hang over both shoulders and upper arms in a cloak-like mass. Page 1 and page 5 show the sleeveless tunic.

minors.description: The script says 'the ragged tunic flap still over his left forearm' in 10.3. In this profile his near (left) forearm is bare skin above the bandage strips, with no tunic flap over it. It does not show the inner face, but the cover device is missing.
minors.evidence: Crop of page 10 at x140-1000, y1255-1635: the near forearm is bare from the elbow to the bandage at about x300-420, y230-290, and the tunic ends at the shoulder.

minors.description: The script lists an iron collar at Nagoji's throat in this close-up, but it is cropped out. In the memory stain, the riders' headgear reads as brown or rust brimmed hats and wraps. The bible rule for background Maratha riders in memory panels is white or cream pagdis, never a rust-red turban.
minors.evidence: Page 10 crop at x940-1700, y905-1250: the frame ends below the chin with no collar showing. Zoomed crop at x190-500, y960-1070: the lead rider wears a rust-brown wrapped hat and the riders behind wear brown brimmed hats.

minors.description: A background prisoner has a red smear across his forehead that reads as blood, which breaks the no-blood rule.
minors.evidence: Zoomed crop of page 4 at x1150-1330, y1150-1290: the third prisoner from the left, looking up, has a red band across his brow.

minors.description: Standing rule 'no painted frames' is broken. The generated art for 7.4 has its own frame painted in: a white strip about 10 px wide plus a dark rule, running inside the lettered panel border down the full left and right edges. It reads as a double border that no other panel in the chapter has.
minors.evidence: page-07.png (1838x2775 px): on row y=2200, x=148-151 is the black page border, x=152-161 is near-white (255,252,244), and x=162-163 is a dark painted rule. The same pattern repeats on every sampled row from y=1888 to y=2536. The right edge mirrors it, with a white strip at x=1676-1685 before the border at x=1686. An automated scan found this on no other panel.

minors.description: Possible pseudo-text in the art. The two gilded carved cartouches on the stern castle behind Nagoji hold curly gold marks that read like painted glyphs or letters rather than plain scrollwork.
minors.evidence: page-08.png: left cartouche at about x=1223-1273, y=507-533; right cartouche at about x=1462-1508, y=533-567, just above and right of Nagoji's head. Seen at 3x zoom, each is a framed panel of letter-like gold strokes.

minors.description: Possible blood. The third prisoner from the left, a bearded man looking up, has a red-pink smear across his forehead that can read as a bloodied brow. That conflicts with the no-blood rule; nothing in this panel should show injury.
minors.evidence: page-04.png: forehead at about x=1215-1245, y=1180-1200. At 6x zoom it is a distinctly red patch against his otherwise brown skin.

minors.description: Possible noose silhouette. A doubled rope hangs from the overhead beam just left of Nagoji's head, with a thick wrapped knot and a loop under it. At page size, next to a man in an iron collar, it can read as a hangman's coil.
minors.evidence: page-05.png: the rope runs down from the beam at about x=290-340, y=2010-2150; the wrapped knot is at about y=2150-2180, and the loop below it is partly hidden behind Nagoji's raised bandaged hand (about x=280-330, y=2180-2240).

minors.description: The memory stain breaks the flags-and-riders rule: background Maratha riders in memory panels wear white or cream pagdis, never Nagoji's rust-red turban. The lead rider wears a rust-brown wrapped turban with a trailing tail. With his cream tunic this invites reading him as Nagoji, and the script says Nagoji is not among the riders.
minors.evidence: page-10.png: the lead rider's turban at about x=300-330, y=980-1000 samples RGB (143,83,56), rust-brown. The other riders wear cream or brown headgear. The pennant at about x=240, y=1000 is unlettered, so it is fine.

minors.description: The falling guard's costume changes from 7.1 and drifts toward red. In 7.2 he shows maroon-red breeches and red at the sleeves under the buff jerkin; in 7.1 the same guard wears dark brown breeches and cream sleeves. This is not a redcoat read on its own, but it adds red to a Portuguese guard and breaks continuity between adjacent panels.
minors.evidence: page-07.png: the guard between the ladder rungs at about x=380-480, y=1620-1720 shows maroon breeches and upper sleeves. Compare 7.1 at about x=700-900, y=620-800 (brown breeches, cream sleeves).

minors.description: Out of lens, lettering: the balloon order is ambiguous. Nagoji's answer 'If the ship breaks, no musket will save them.' sits at left at nearly the same height as Keshavrao's question at right, so many readers will read the answer first.
minors.evidence: page-02.png: Nagoji's balloon at about x=490-1070, y=1905-2025. Keshavrao's 'Sahib, if the ship breaks...' at about x=1250-1620, y=1830-1950.

minors.description: The guard's two balloons may be read in the wrong order. 'If any of you break your chains...' sits clearly higher than 'Quiet down there...', so it tends to be read first, although the script opens with 'Quiet down there'. Its left edge also clips the brim of the guard's morion.
minors.evidence: 'If any of you...' has its top at about y1180 at the upper right. 'Quiet down...' has its top at about y1297 at the left. The balloon edge overlaps the morion brim at about (600,1250).

minors.description: The sailors' storm shouts are lettered in smooth round balloons with tiny nub tails. The script asks for jagged, overlapping shout balloons, so the panic of the off-panel orders does not come through.
minors.evidence: Page 1, top-right panel of the second tier: two smooth pill balloons, 'Reef the sails!...' and 'Tie that down!...', each with a small triangular nub at the top.

minors.description: The script tags Nagoji's orders '(in Marathi)', but the lettering carries no language marker such as angle brackets. The 'Hold to the beams!' balloon also hides his second forearm hooked over the timber, which is half of the grip the panel is meant to show.
minors.evidence: The balloon at about x690-1085, y560-688 covers the area where Nagoji's raised left arm meets the beam. Only fingertips show at its left edge, at about (690,580).

minors.description: The narration order is ambiguous. The second caption, 'To them I was just another piece of loose cargo...', at the right sits higher than the first, 'The storm greeted me...', at the left.
minors.evidence: The left caption's top is at about y295 and the right caption's top at about y260, both in the same tier.

minors.description: The script places the caption 'For a moment I was nowhere...' inside the upper-left inset of Nagoji's hand. It is lettered over the main image above Keshavrao instead, which ties Nagoji's dazed first-person moment to Keshavrao's image.
minors.evidence: The caption spans about x748-1155, y262-352 in the main panel. The inset is at x108-443.

minors.description: Nagoji's balloon 'Tie it! Around your chest! Quick!' is jammed flush against the left panel border and reads before the caption, which the script places first. The caption sits over the middle of the deck, where the short-landing throw should read.
minors.evidence: The balloon's left edge is on the frame line at x about 110, y683-770. The caption spans x597-995, y745-838, between the two men.

minors.description: There is an awkward crop at the top-left corner: a sliver of Nagoji's face, just a moustache and chin, is sliced by the panel border.
minors.evidence: Page 9, third panel, top-left corner at about x108-170, y940-975.

minors.description: The caption 'Keshavrao was gone.' crowds Nagoji's right hand: its left edge touches the thumb tip.
minors.evidence: The caption spans about x963-1175, y1598-1662. The thumb tip is at about (960,1660).

minors.description: The 'Forgive me.' balloon sits over the front of Nagoji's chest, where he pulls the rope knot tight. The knot-tightening action is partly hidden.
minors.evidence: The balloon spans about x512-668, y1040-1125, over the rope wraps and his left hand at the front of his torso.

minors.description: The art does not fill the frame. A white keyline, a double border, runs inside the frame on the left, right and bottom, unlike the other panels on the page.
minors.evidence: Crops of page 7 at display x95-240 and x1100-1230, y1340-1560, and the bottom edge at y1760-1845. There is a white strip about 8-10 display px wide between the outer frame at x108 and x1217 and the inner art edge at about x118 and x1207.

minors.description: The guard's two lines risk being read out of order. The second line's balloon sits higher than the first.
minors.evidence: 'If any of you break your chains...' is at the upper right, starting about 115 px (display) above 'Quiet down there. No shouting. No prayers.' at the left, and their heights overlap. The script order is 'Quiet down there' first.

minors.description: The script asks for jagged, overlapping shout balloons from above. The lettering uses standard smooth oval balloons, set side by side and not overlapping.
minors.evidence: 'Reef the sails! Haul, haul!' and 'Tie that down! Move, you son of a dog!' are round, smooth balloons with small tails pointing up, and they do not overlap.

minors.description: Nagoji hooks only one arm over the beam, not both forearms with his manacled wrists together over the wood as the script says. His orders also carry no Marathi indicator, though the script tags them as spoken in Marathi.
minors.evidence: Only Nagoji's right arm is raised to the timber. His left arm hangs down under the tunic flap. The balloons read plainly 'Hold to the beams! Hook your arms over the wood.' and 'Do not let the chain drag you.' with no language tag or bracket convention.

minors.description: The broadside hit is not conveyed. There is no sideways throw, no weightless moment, and no chains snapping sideways along the rows. Instead, water flows down a central aisle while the men hold steady in their pens.
minors.evidence: The panel shows a long aisle with surf running away from camera and prisoners braced or seated behind the pen boards. Nobody is displaced and no chain is moving.

minors.description: The script calls for a wide shot frozen in a harsh lightning flash. The art is a half-width panel in even, dim blue light, with men sitting in a row looking up rather than clinging to beams and to each other.
minors.evidence: Panel 4.3 shares a tier with 4.2 at half width. The light is a soft blue glow from the seams with no flash. Most of the men sit with their hands in their laps.

minors.description: The script puts the first balloon upper left, before the impact, and the second lower right, after it. Both balloons are at the top of the panel at the same height, so the before-and-after timing is lost.
minors.evidence: 'The mainmast! Cut the rope...' and 'She is taking water! Pump...' sit side by side along the top edge, at about y 1165 (display).

minors.description: The art does not fill the panel frame. There are unpainted white strips inside the border.
minors.evidence: A white vertical strip about 10 px wide runs inside the left border, at about x 150 to 165 in the original page pixels, for the full height of the panel. A matching strip runs inside the right border.

minors.description: The narration caption is not in the inset as the script specifies. Keshavrao's wrists show no connecting chain, which undercuts the 'slack of the wrist chain' and the 9.3 beat where the chain catches on the rope. His right hand reads as bracing, not as reaching for an absent sword.
minors.evidence: 'For a moment I was nowhere...' is at the top right over Keshavrao, and the upper-left inset of Nagoji's hand in the rope coil has no text. Each of Keshavrao's cuffs trails a separate short chain end, with his hands about 500 px apart. His right hand hangs toward the deck with the fingers down.

minors.description: The top-left corner is an awkward crop. A sliver of Nagoji's moustache and jaw is clipped by the frame, which reads as a stray fragment rather than 'Nagoji's hands at the edge of the frame'.
minors.evidence: Part of a moustache and chin shows at the extreme top-left corner of 9.3, about (150 to 230, 1310) in the original page pixels, above the bandaged hands holding the rope.

minors.description: Nagoji is looking down at his own palms, not at the empty hatch. The ladder is intact, though the script says 'the broken ladder'.
minors.evidence: Nagoji's head is bowed toward his open hands at the left. The ladder at the right, inside the hatch, is whole, with even rungs.

minors.description: The memory's key image, riders galloping on past the fallen comrade, is mostly hidden behind the two captions. Only the fallen horse and man read clearly.
minors.evidence: The riders are visible only as a faint sliver at the top left. The caption 'In the Deccan, before we rode into Portuguese fire...' covers most of them, and the second caption covers the space between the riders and the fallen man.
